title: Updating a live demo fetches and verifies the new release first; a failed download leaves the old demo serving
steps: S1: From the repo root at the commit under test, with TEST_DATABASE_URL set to a Postgres: node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern="cannot be fetched|published while the update was fetching|polling follows the demo" apps/tracy-web/test/ops-demos.test.mjs
S3: Read the ok/not ok line of each test.
expect: Every test reports ok: a live demo's update asks /_host/prefetch and never /_host/teardown while the prefetch runs or after it fails; the site row stays published with its port; /api/ops/demos still reports the demo live with the failed job's reason (403); a release published mid-fetch stops the update with nothing torn down; a done prefetch asks one teardown keyed by its job; quickstart.py --prefetch fills the cache, names a spent GitHub quota with its reset time and waits out a short Retry-After (pre-fix: the teardown was asked at the press, and a 403 at the download left the address blank).
evidence: 25/10/2026 dev: ja-boxing-joomla teardown 08:55:51-08:56:22, provision failed 08:56:26 and 08:59:51 with 'quickstart download failed (HTTP 403)', success at 09:09; tracy-web logged 'GitHub rate limit exhausted for this token until 2026-10-25T09:05:13Z'.
fence: apps/tracy-web/src/ops/demos.js installOnHost (live branch) + apps/tracy-web/src/lib/demo-update.js replaceAfterPrefetch + apps/tracy-host/src/prefetch.js + quickstart.py prefetch/open_release.

cmd: --test-name-pattern=cannot be fetched|published while the update was fetching|polling follows the demo
tests: an update whose new release cannot be fetched leaves the live demo serving, and says why
a release published while the update was fetching stops it before anything comes down
polling follows the demo through provision, going public, and a fresh redeploy
